rounds.text: Wagend Infra Venture Ltd trades at a substantial discount to its asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.59x at a share price of ₹ 1.15 against a book value of ₹ 1.96 [E2], and favourably compares to the sector benchmark P/B of 1.51x [E7]. The business demonstrates explosive top-line acceleration, delivering compounded sales growth of 43% over 10 years, 45% over 5 years, 52% over 3 years, and a massive 465% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16, E17]. This immense revenue momentum is successfully translating into bottom-line expansion, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 50% [E21] and a recent quarterly sales increase [E59]. The market is failing to price in this accelerating earnings trajectory [E60], which is further evidenced by profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 33% as the company begins to outperform expectations [E52]. Conceded: the trailing P/E ratio sits at an elevated 181x [E1] and 122x against a sector benchmark of 19.94x [E6], five-year profit growth has contracted by 21% [E19], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4].

The bull relies heavily on the asset discount of a 0.59x price-to-book ratio [E2] and a 0.62x sector comparison [E7], but ignores that this asset backing generates an extremely weak return on assets of just 0.27% compared to a sector benchmark of 1.54% [E8]. While the bull points to explosive trailing sales growth of 465% [E17], it glosses over the severe structural decay in longer-term profitability, specifically the 21% contraction in compounded profit growth over five years [E19]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has accelerated across multiple timeframes [E14, E15, E16, E17] and trailing profit growth reached 50% [E21], but this earnings expansion has pushed the trailing P/E ratio to an extreme 181x [E1] and 122x against a sector benchmark of only 19.94x [E6]. This massive valuation multiple is entirely unsupported by a stagnant three-year profit growth rate of 0% [E20] and a complete lack of shareholder return through a 0.00% dividend yield [E4].
